topic: Mohe 1997 gravity anomaly — verification of c11 H1+H2 self-applied patches (Unnikrishnan scope tighten + kappa arithmetic fix)
our_argument_summary: WIN-011 documents the dome silently relocating its Mohe gravity claim (V51.0: −6.5 μGal at eclipse maximum, a phase its own sources report as null) to ~7.0 ± 2.7 μGal at first/last contact (live page since 2026-04-17), exactly where Wang et al. (2000) had already located the data. The Unnikrishnan (2001) citation is shown to be selective (data-as-evidence framing post-patch), the thermal-tilt loophole is author-conceded, SG instruments already recorded nulls (Mansinha et al. 2001), and the κ=1.67 coupling fails the dome's 5% tolerance on the dome's own rewritten value (10.9/7.0=1.557, 6.8% error). Verdict: Not Demonstrated.

h1_scope_tighten.evidence: detail_evidence now reads 'rules out the 1997 data as evidence for the dome's mechanism in the same breath, and treats the contact-phase valleys as conventional rather than evidence of new gravity at all' (data/wins.json:WIN-011.detail_evidence). detail_verdict_text now uses the data-as-evidence framing: 'that paper rules out the 1997 data as evidence for the dome's mechanism in the same breath — the dome cannot invoke Unnikrishnan against the globe's shielding hypothesis while claiming the same dataset is anomalous for its own coupling'. The over-claim phrases 'rules out the dome's own mechanism' and 'any new gravitational property' are absent from all six user-visible fields (grep-verified this run).

h2_kappa_arithmetic.evidence: detail_evidence and detail_verdict_text both state 'a 6.8% error against 1.67'; detail_extra states '6.8% off'. Recomputed this run: |10.9/7.0 − 1.67|/1.67 = 6.76% → rounds to 6.8 (percentage and denominator now agree). The stale 7.25/7.26 figures are absent (grep-verified). Companion figures re-verified: 10.9/6.5=1.6769 (0.41% vs 1.67); ±2.7 μGal span 10.9/9.7=1.124 to 10.9/4.3=2.535 matches the quoted κ 1.12–2.53.

holes_found.description: Residual scope over-read in one subordinate clause, same family as c11 H1 but narrower: detail_evidence still says Unnikrishnan et al. 'rule out both, using Wang et al.'s own before-and-after-eclipse record to set the tightest terrestrial bound ever measured on any such anomalous coupling'. The paper's quantitative bound is on the gravitational SHIELDING (Majorana extinction) parameter specifically — c11's own search evidence quoted 'constrain the characteristic shielding parameter to the lowest bound ever from a terrestrial experiment'. Attaching 'tightest terrestrial bound ever measured' to 'any such anomalous coupling' re-creates, in miniature, the symmetry exposure H1 flagged: a defender can say the numerical bound does not parameterize an electromagnetic-gravitational coupling. 'They rule out both' is defensible under the data-as-evidence framing (the paper concludes the 1997 data evidence neither hypothesis), but the bound clause is not.
holes_found.recommendation: One-clause edit: '...to set the tightest terrestrial bound ever measured on gravitational shielding — and to conclude the 1997 record evidences no anomalous signal of either kind' (or simply end the sentence at 'rule out both' and let the existing next sentence carry the weight). Keeps the point, drops the last over-attachment.

kernel_of_truth.description: The patched text now gives the dome its due cleanly: the rewritten WIN-011 is more honest than V51.0 — correct magnitude with uncertainty, correct phases, an author-conceded loophole, and a dated falsifiable SG test (data/wins.json:WIN-011.detail_evidence, 'The rewritten version is more honest — credit where due' paragraph). That concession survives both patches intact.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A label that says CONFIRMED while conceding an open thermal-tilt loophole and deferring resolution to an unrun 2026-08-12 test is pending, not confirmed — and the dome's own coupling check now fails on the dome's own rewritten value (data/wins.json:WIN-011.detail_verdict_text, κ 6.8% > 5% tolerance).

summary_for_decider: Both ISS-2680 (H1 scope tighten) and ISS-2681 (H2 kappa arithmetic) verified landed cleanly; no regression, no new inconsistency across finding/detail_evidence/detail_verdict_text/detail_extra/tldr fields; arithmetic recomputed and correct. One MINOR residual: the 'tightest terrestrial bound ever measured on any such anomalous coupling' clause still over-attaches Unnikrishnan's shielding-specific bound — one-clause fix recommended. Carry-over note per 7c: this residual is a narrowed restatement of c11 H1, but ISS-2680 is CLOSED — no matching open issue exists; decider should create one (or fold the one-clause fix into the next WIN-011 touch). Verdict Not Demonstrated holds.
deeper_analysis: Verification scope per queue class. Checks performed: (1) grep for old over-claim phrasings across all user-visible WIN-011 fields — absent; (2) presence and wording of both replacement phrasings — present, match c11 recommendations near-verbatim; (3) full κ arithmetic recompute (0.41%, 6.76%→6.8, span 1.124–2.535) — all consistent; (4) cross-field consistency: finding, detail_extra, tldr_evidence, tldr_verdict all carry the same numbers and the same data-as-evidence framing — no field was left on the old framing; (5) code tags unchanged and still correct (hardcoded/post_hoc). The single residual clause predates the patch and sat outside H1's literal recommendation — flagged at minor because the main symmetry exposure (the headline 'rules out the dome's own mechanism' sentence readers quote) is gone, and the remaining clause is subordinate, mid-paragraph, and partially shielded by the adjacent corrected sentence.
